citations.F1: `serialize_event` issues one `SELECT ... FROM users WHERE id = $1` per event — 1,000 sequential round trips on one pooled connection; fetch all actors once with `WHERE id = ANY($1)`
citations.F2: Dedupe uses `if ev["dedupe_key"] in seen` against a list — O(n²), ~1.8M comparisons at 1,912 rows
citations.F3: `lookup_geo` calls blocking `requests.get` (2 s timeout) inside the async handler, freezing the whole worker's event loop
citations.F4: filtering 4.2M rows by `org_id` + `created_at` is a scan plus sort; add `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY events_org_created_idx ON events (org_id, created_at DESC)`
citations.F5: `_request_timings` grows forever, one float per request across all routes ... replace with a bounded `deque(maxlen=...)`
citations.F6: `_geo_cache` is an unbounded dict keyed by client IP with no eviction — a second, slower leak; bound it (TTL or LRU with a max size)
citations.F7: Baseline before editing: `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS)` the events SELECT with acme's params ($1=4127, 30 d), and time the endpoint 5× warm against acme — record median and spread; re-run both after every change below.
citations.F9: Do not ship the on-call proposal. 16 workers × pool max 50 × 6 pods = 4,800 Postgres connections ... The Redis part is also near-useless as specified
citations.F11: `since` defaults to `now() - 30d`, so the resolved cache key is different on every request and hits ~0%
